runtimes.cuda: CUDA RTX A5000 / vLLM 0.26 / Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct fp16
runtimes.metal: Metal M3 Ultra / llama.cpp / Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct Q4_K_M

finding: The two runtimes win at opposite ends and the crossover is sharp. Metal answers first-token in 14.4ms against CUDA's 181ms at concurrency 1 -- it is local, with no network hop -- but collapses to a 5.0s TTFT at concurrency 16 because llama.cpp has no continuous batching. CUDA holds TTFT flat at 313ms while scaling 11.7x to 1617 tok/s aggregate. Routing interactive single-user work to local Metal and batch work to rented CUDA is therefore not a preference, it is what the measurements require.
why_a_homogeneous_fleet_cannot_copy_this: A provider that owns one class of hardware can only move work between instances of the same shape. The crossover above needs two physically different machines with opposite strengths, one of which is not in any datacenter.
comparability_caveat: Different models and precision: 3B Q4_K_M on Metal, 1.5B fp16 on CUDA. Absolute throughput is NOT comparable between them. What is comparable, because both are model-independent, is the SHAPE: the TTFT gap at concurrency 1 is dominated by local-vs-network round trip, and the collapse at 16 is an engine property (llama.cpp has no continuous batching, vLLM does). A like-for-like absolute comparison still needs identical weights and precision on both sides.
